# jsonld-knowledge-graph

> A Claude Code skill (instructions plus one bundled lint script, MIT, v0.1.0) that designs and ships a companion JSON-LD knowledge graph (`graph.jsonld`) next to `llms.txt` for projects with stable concept-level structure. Encodes domain entities and relationships as schema.org triples so LLM search engines (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude) get the relationships as explicit statements and can resolve the project's entities. Pairs with `llms-txt-writer` (which owns prose / navigator wording).

Status: active, synced one way from the author's Claude Code harness by `scripts/sync-from-local.sh` (it never commits), so this repository can trail the harness between syncs. The skill sits in the author's [Authorship Strategy](https://github.com/shimo4228/authorship-strategy) line (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20263316); the author's practice lines are listed on the hub [shimo4228](https://github.com/shimo4228/shimo4228).

## Core documentation

- [SKILL.md](skills/jsonld-knowledge-graph/SKILL.md): full skill specification (in Japanese) — when-to-use gate, concept-layer-only boundary (file-level structure is derived from code, never stored), 9 reusable design moves, schema vocabulary design criteria, cross-graph `@id` discipline, bilingual strategy, companion file wiring, lint-based verification workflow, a pointer to a separate `hf-sync` skill for the Hugging Face mirror, maintenance contract
- [graph_lint.py](skills/jsonld-knowledge-graph/scripts/graph_lint.py): the bundled lint (`uv run --with pyld python3`); reports DROPPED-KEY, URL-LITERAL, VOLATILE, and NAME-DRIFT across several graphs; exit 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 fatal
- [inspiration.md](skills/jsonld-knowledge-graph/inspiration.md): origin story and canonical implementation pointers (kept separate from `SKILL.md` for portability)
- [README.md](README.md): human-facing narrative (when to use, install, how it works, key concept, what it does not do, verification)
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): release notes (v0.1.0 initial release)

## The 9 design moves

The skill prescribes nine reusable moves that turn an ad-hoc JSON-LD file into a stable, LLM-citable artifact:

1. Dual `@type` on every node (custom namespace + schema.org base)
2. Language-tagged literals for bilingual (`@language` per `@value`, single file for en/ja)
3. Schema absence enforces forbidden relationships (don't define edge types you must never use)
4. Cross-graph `@id` reuse so JSON-LD processors merge triples across files
5. Volatile state (version, count, churning enums) excluded at schema level
6. Matrix encoding via paired complementary edges (e.g. `appliesTo` + `realizedBy`)
7. Root `Dataset` node so crawlers see the graph's purpose and entry points
8. Reading-order block in `llms.txt` directing AI to read `graph.jsonld` first
9. Reverse-link from line repos to hub graph in hub-and-spoke topology

## Hugging Face Datasets mirror sync

After a `graph.jsonld` edit, `SKILL.md` suggests also uploading the graph to a Hugging Face Datasets mirror, which HF auto-converts to Parquet so the graph loads from `pandas` / `Polars` / `Datasets`. The procedure, prerequisites, repo mapping and token scope belong to a separate `hf-sync` skill that this repository does not include; it is published in [claude-harness](https://github.com/shimo4228/claude-harness/tree/main/skills/hf-sync). The step sends the file outside your machine.

## Standard reference

- [llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org/): Answer.AI's `llms.txt` proposal (Jeremy Howard, 2024) — the two-file `llms.txt` + `llms-full.txt` layout this skill's companion-file wiring extends
- [schema.org](https://schema.org/): the base vocabulary the graph's nodes anchor to (`Dataset`, `ScholarlyArticle`, `DefinedTerm`, `SoftwareSourceCode`, etc.)
- [JSON-LD 1.1](https://www.w3.org/TR/json-ld11/): the `@id` reuse and triple-merge behavior the skill depends on

## Sibling skills

- [llms-txt-writer](https://github.com/shimo4228/llms-txt-writer): owns prose / navigator wording for `llms.txt` / `llms-full.txt`. Reads this skill's reading-order block requirement.
- [readme-writer](https://github.com/shimo4228/readme-writer): owns how the README points to `graph.jsonld` and `llms.txt` (a plain line at the end).
- [context-sync](https://github.com/shimo4228/context-sync): audits drift between `graph.jsonld` and prose docs, and project doc role overlap / freshness (Maintain phase).
- [search-first](https://github.com/shimo4228/search-first): research-before-coding workflow.
- [claude-skill-writing-ecosystem](https://github.com/shimo4228/claude-skill-writing-ecosystem): human-facing writing orchestrator (different concern: human readers, not AI crawlers).
